# Declaration test resources

These files support the tests for **Preferences > General > Suppress automatic entity
declarations when saving**, in `org.protege.editor.owl.model.declaration`.

## corpus/ and baseline/

`baseline/` records what Protege writes with the preference off, which is what Protege has
always written. `DeclarationBaseline_TestCase` renders every corpus ontology to every format
the preference reaches, reads the declarations back, and compares them with the baseline.

The comparison is on declaration sets, not on document text. Prefix order and the OWL API's
"generated by" comment move for reasons that have nothing to do with declarations.

| | |
|---|---|
| Corpus | 5 ontologies, copied from `src/test/resources/ontologies` |
| Formats | RDF/XML (`.rdf`), Turtle (`.ttl`), OWL/XML (`.owx`), Functional (`.ofn`) |
| Baseline documents | 20 |

Two rules govern the corpus, and both were learned the hard way:

- every member carries entities. An ontology with none cannot carry a declaration, so it
  cannot detect a change to declarations;
- every member renders deterministically. `photography.owl` does not, and is deliberately
  absent: the OWL API cannot type 31 of its datatypes and mints
  `http://org.semanticweb.owlapi/error#ErrorNN` entities for them from a counter that keeps
  climbing for the life of the JVM.

The corpus is a copy on purpose. The ontologies under `ontologies/` belong to other tests,
which are free to edit them; a baseline that followed those edits would report a change to
declarations that never happened.

### Regenerating

**A baseline diff is a finding to explain, not a file to overwrite.** If the comparison fails,
the question is what changed the output, not how to make the test green again.

When a change to the output is intended and understood, `DeclarationBaseline.main` rewrites
every baseline document. It needs the module directory as its working directory.
